decisions.interpretation: The initial unstressed a occupies the first note position. The remaining part of the word occupies the final note position, retaining the received spelling. These are compressed note groups, not a claim that the words have only two spoken syllables. No pitches, note timings, or diplomatic text were changed.

evidence.observation: Psalm 2:6 prints both appointed and anointed underlined. This supports special compression, but does not print the exact note-by-note division used here.
The referenced Dundee score, attributed to the Scottish Psalter of 1615, contains notes but no lyrics. It cannot directly verify this Psalm 2 word underlay.
The TCP transcription of the named 1650 witness preserves appointed and anointed in Psalm II without an explicit musical underlay.

decisions.rationale: The two existing note positions must not group the beginning and stressed stem together and then isolate the unstressed ed ending on the cadence. Separating the initial a better follows the words’ stress. The precise division remains an editorial interpretation rather than a verified historic score transcription.
